correctness.rationale: Exact line search makes consecutive residuals orthogonal. In dimension two their normalized directions give an orthonormal basis; writing A in this basis as [s t; t q], the reciprocals of the first two steps are s and q. Cayley–Hamilton gives r2 = rho b, with rho = t²/(sq) in [0,1). Scale invariance then gives even iterates (1−rho^m)A⁻¹b and odd iterates equal to these plus alpha0 rho^m b, all nonnegative. A zero residual terminates (including b=0); dimension one terminates in at most one step. For the witness the leading minors are 2, 2 and 12 and the off-diagonal graph is connected. The first line search gives 2/5. With r1=(3,14,−9)/5, Ar1=(−22,45,−77)/5, hence alpha1=286/1257 and x2,3=−4/419. Multiplication by A confirms the displayed strictly positive solution. The first step cannot lose sign in any dimension. Reviewed RESULT.md, VERIFICATION.md, verify.py and its recorded CHECK_OUTPUT.txt; the judgments above follow from the proof and exact arithmetic, not the recorded success line or a new run.
